Rough and raw graphing of historical data with Rickshaw.  Still need to add in the bits to get a list of historical dates available, redraw graph when data changes, etc.  Also need to/want to explore HTML5 canvas for the hover detail rendering because SVG slows down paint events on Chrome like whoa and makes the hover detail rubber band when you move the cursor too fast.

Added endpoint that serves the timestamp/thread count pairs for all snapshots for a given day.  Reworked some of the filestore/snapshot code to make it cleaner and support grabbing that data.  Made a very rough first pass at actually graphing the data - still needs the proper hover detail labels, needs code to handle clicks on the graph translating to loading the given snapshot, etc etc.  Added a HTTP endpoint for pprof debugging at localhost:6060 when you run Cadastre with the --debug flag.
Starting to add in placeholders and some CSS for the historical stuff.  Switched to jsDelivr for CDNable assets as it's a wee bit faster than cdnjs.

Change around the storage interface, and the file store, to provide retrieval methods that match the actions performed in the UI.  Implement retrieving a single snapshot based on server internal name and timestampp.
Add in Rickshaw to the index template and add a stub method for handling individual time period snapshot requests.
Implemented support for query length limiting finally.

Merge pull request #2 from chuck/master

Update for Percona Server 5.6, including removing ROWS_READ for all vari...
Fixed a syntax error and fixed some quirks with switching between the real-time and historical views.

Lots of tweaking to the UI.  Removed a lot of useless crap to really hone in on what's important.  Updated/fixed a lot of view state issues - spinner showing without hiding the current data, database selection and query states not working together correctly, etc.
Update the main binary to import the githubized version of the project so that 'go get' is all that is needed to grab the project.
Switched to my own key/value cache and back to howeyc for fsnotify.
Tweaked the recent data link format so the pills weren't so long and it wouldn't linebreak on ~1200-1300px wide displays.
Worked out the real-time view options and layout.  Got the links working so it displays the historical data as you click on different past snapshots.

Added support for filtering the queries based on sleeping/locked/etc.  Added some basics to support keeping the last N real-time reloads around so you can toggle back and forth to display them.  Updated same-server reloads to not blast away the events header/view options stuff and instead simply reload the events table.

Modularized more of the event content loading.  Refreshing a server's data now happens independently of the header (server name / time) and view options (real-time vs historical, etc).  Added the first piece of the real-time refresh - a reload button.  Still need to add data history (to allow you to switch back to the last N real-time reloads you did for comparison) and need to add the basics of the 'historical' view.  Still need to add thread counts, with type breakdown, as well.

Start modularizing some of the JS that builds the content within the page.  This is so that we can update parts of the page independently - making switching historical time ranges faster and allowing us to do things like auto-refresh without redrawing everything below the navbars every single time.

Added more JSON hinting to snapshot structs.  Finally displaying process list events in the UI.  Added the skeleton markup for the real-time/historical switcher and where the historical graphs will live.  Added coloring for normal/locked/sleeping queries.

Added some better error output for when the configuration loads a duplicate server entry.  Updated the format of the configuration to change 'category' to 'groupName' for servers.  Generate the list of server groups, with servers per group, when reading the configuration and not at the time of the request.  Use JSON hints on the server/server group structs to make JSON encoding easy peasy.
Added the logic to take a snapshot for a specific database server.  Right now, it returns the JSON encoded version of the Snapshot struct but the UI doesn't handle it yet.
Changed the listening address to be a configured-specified value instead of hard-coded.
Fixed a JS error that didn't properly use the group name when building the server dropdown.
Remove unused static assets.

Added gzip support to normal responses.  Doesn't affect static content.  Switched Bootstrap/jQuery assets to load from CDNJS, since CDNJS is faster than anything I'm going to whip together in this project for serving static assets. Server groups endpoint now returns valid data instead of dummy data.
Update language in doc.go to show that Cadastre supports real-time polling of databases along with historical data.

Added a real favicon as a base64 encoded constant - less files to read from disk. Switched to gorilla/mux for the HTTP router to get parameterized route matching.  Added basic endpoints for getting the server groups and for getting a current snapshot from a given server - both endpoints are returning errors or mock data currently.  Wrote a lot of the UI and backing JS.  Added error messages for timeouts, handling of errors from the server, etc.

Switch to 'go fmt' formatting.  It's the Go(tm) way.  Switch to using html/template instead of HAML as this way there's less external library dependence and no need to fix someone else's incomplete library.  Only invalidate the cache on modifications, so that deleted templates (which should be rare during actual operation) still get served out of cache until the daemon is restarted or until another template is modified.
Update the web server to work with the new, forked version of gohaml.
Adding .gitignore file to ignore binaries generated during testing and potentially other stuff.

Starting to add the wrappings of a usable piece of software.  Added the actual binary source to generate a binary that will run the damn thing.  Got the basic header for the index page in there and tweaked the syntax for the Haml library I'm using.  Added static resources.  Added an example configuration file.

First major commit for Cadastre.  The snapshot fetcher works but needs a lot of love and actual testing to work out any edge cases and properly handle failure/errors.  The web UI portion still needs a ton of actual feature implementation but the basics of the HTTP server are there... although that may change if I find a better package to handle that portion.

Boom.  Simple way to run commands while making sure you can't pre-maturely run them if you fat finger <enter> before finishing the command.  You also get a chance to review the command to see if you actually fat fingered that portion.
